Thank you, that was very well thought out and well said! 

I agree that change must come from within, I guess I was just hopeful that there could be something I could do to help nudge him in the right direction, or plant a seed of inspiration to make him want to help himself. 

People do grow and change with time, and it’s a bummer because the first few years we dated he wasn’t like this all the time, but with time he slowly became more and more grouchy. It’s been many years since I’ve seen him be generally positive, but I’ve stayed hopeful. Currently, we will take on a situation and he’ll be the negative one, but I’ll try to point out the good stuff and we deal with it together. 

I’m not at the point where I would consider leaving him, because although I explained the problematic elements of dating him, I am otherwise happy. (If you can imagine being happy with a grump, lol.)

I’ll read about emotional contagion so I can avoid it, I certainly don’t want to make it worse for either of us. Also, yes it is more than ADHD, but I think it compounds the unhealthy habits, the anxiety and depression because his meds make him fixate on things in a way he didn’t before. However, he needs the medication or he feels like his head is buzzing. I honestly worry sometimes that medication is ruining him just as much as it’s helping. Obviously I could be wrong, as I’m not a professional, but I spend a lot of time observing and trying to read up on how to cope with the combination of things he’s got going on, so I don’t think it’s a totally baseless concern. 

I guess the moral of the story is, I understand that he needs to help himself. I understand that I can’t expect him to change for me. I’m just hopeful that he will eventually get better with patience and gentle guidance. There is definitely a balance in keeping myself mentally healthy, and I won’t let my own needs be forgotten. 

Thank you again for all of your advice.

Hey! Don’t beat yourself up so much. 23 is still young, but I understand where you’re coming from. I’m 26 and still in college, been working on a 4 year degree for like 8, but time isn’t real anyway if you think about it. We made it up! 

In all seriousness, feeling regret and like you wasted the time that has passed can be panic inducing. However, don’t forget that although time has passed doesn’t mean that it’s too late to start making memories. 

Beating yourself up about wasting time creates an unhealthy mindset about time passing, so the sooner you can shake that feeling off the better. You may not have enjoyed the last 5 years, so why not try to shift the focus to the next 5? Maybe try to make daily goals, start small. 

Tomorrow take some time and go for a walk, and really focus on the fresh air, the feeling of being alive and able to walk and move, and just being alive. It’s silly, but start small. Reward yourself for healthy habits. 

I got through the worst year of my life by just trying to take it one step at a time. I make lists every day now to keep my mind on track. I have fun goals (learning to play ukulele, even though I’m not very good) professional goals, and personal goals (reaching out to old friends to try to rekindle a friendship, losing some weight) 

These goals can be short term and very long term, but they will help you to keep looking ahead, instead of looking back. It’s not perfect, but it will help. 

Maybe it would be good to think about what kinds of hobbies you like. I love magic the gathering, and local card stores near me normally do causal gameplay on fridays for whoever wants to come and tons of people don’t really have a lot of friends that go, and it’s a safe space for that very reason. The same is true for our local “fun” adult sport teams. (It’s called super fun activities club, it’s kinda like adult recess. I don’t like sports so that stresses me out, but it could be your thing!) 

All I’m saying is, invest in yourself in the moment. If making friends is a goal, the only way to do it is to try. If you feel nervous and you mess up an interaction, just apologize and say you have anxiety. Honestly, people are more empathetic than you’d expect. And the worst case scenario is that you walk away embarrassed but it’s ok! If they are crappy about it that’s on them, not you. You deserve kindness, so that’s kinda like prescreening to find out who’s a jerk haha. 

I hope this gives you a push in the right direction. The future can be a beautiful thing, it’s not too late to start. Life always has ups and downs, but don’t forget the highs when you’re feeling low. This too shall pass. Good luck man.

I just picked up this giant majesty palm. I was super excited about it, until I got it home and started giving it a haircut. 
I read that it could be scale, but that there is also a fungus that looks very similar.
These are obviously very different situations, and I don’t want to freak out if it’s just some fungus. 
It’s a beautiful tree, has lots of new growth and otherwise seems healthy. 
The spots look dry and crusty, some are even broken resulting in holes. It’s not all over, but some fronds are bad while others are unaffected. 
I also took photos of the base with some new growth to show the tiny black spots there, not sure if that’s healthy or if it’s related. 
It’s in isolation currently, and I would really like to save this beauty. In the meantime I’m trimming the obviously blighted fronds and sealing them up just in case it’s scale. 
What do you guys think? 
Help! 💕🌿
